content.intro: In this lesson, work through **Numerical Data Types and Precision** using the syllabus terms **Integer and floating-point types** and **Single versus double precision**. Start from a clearly stated numerical question, choose the smallest appropriate SciPy tool, and inspect the result rather than treating the returned number as self-validating.
content.why_it_matters: Numerical Data Types and Precision supports reliable scientific computing by turning a mathematical or data-analysis problem into a repeatable computation. It is useful when you need to choose between methods, understand assumptions, and report limits rather than merely produce a number.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: **Numerical Data Types and Precision** is best approached as a deliberate numerical workflow. The supplied curriculum highlights **Integer and floating-point types**, along with **Single versus double precision**, **Complex-valued arrays**, **Type conversion**. Define what the inputs mean and what result would count as credible before increasing problem size or complexity.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about the method
content_blocks.text: Connect the mathematics to the documented API family **floating-point tolerance**. Check input shape and dtype, units and domain assumptions, and whether the method is exact, approximate, iterative, or statistical. The output should be accompanied by an error estimate or a separate check when the API provides one or when the problem allows it.

content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the quantity the code computes. Change one input or parameter and predict what should happen before re-running. For an iterative solver, also inspect its status and stopping criteria.

common_mistakes.problem: Choosing an algorithm before stating the problem and assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Two algorithms that look similar can have different domains, stability, performance, and convergence behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down input shape, units/domain, the quantity to compute, and a validation check before selecting an API.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating returned values as exact truths.
common_mistakes.why: Floating-point arithmetic and iterative numerical algorithms use finite precision and stopping conditions.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect success/status fields and error estimates where available; use scale-appropriate tolerances and independent checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying an example without checking version or edge cases.
common_mistakes.why: Signatures and legacy status can change between releases, and example data rarely covers boundary behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the installed SciPy version, official documentation, input constraints, and a failure case.
